page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-2 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration within the general-purpose N2 series. It provides 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical Intel Xeon core running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz with hyperthreading enabled. The configuration is paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an elevated allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The underlying x86_64 processor includes support for instruction set extensions such as AVX-512F and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware-accelerated AES cryptography and 33 MB of shared L3 cache. There are no integrated GPUs and no local storage drives attached by default.

Benchmark measurements reflect the constraints of its two-thread, single-core CPU footprint. In synthetic evaluation, stress-ng registers a single-core score of 1827.69 in the middle tier, whereas multi-core throughput scores 1875.88 in the lower tier due to thread contention over a single core. Geekbench records single-core and multi-core ratings of 1099.0 and 1321.0 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests yield 13.86 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 11.77 GB/sec for write operations on large data blocks. In application scenarios, the instance achieves 1.67 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.61 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

Cost efficiency is focused around memory-heavy footprints that do not require substantial parallel computing power. Compared to standard balanced configurations, the 1:8 core-to-RAM ratio prevents overprovisioning vCPUs when only memory footprint matters. The primary tradeoff lies in raw computation: CPU-bound, multi-threaded pipelines will experience significant execution bottlenecks on a single hyperthreaded physical core.

Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-2 is appropriate for lightweight in-memory caching layers, modest database instances, microservices with medium memory usage, and background ETL or data ingestion jobs with moderate processing requirements.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-2 is a memory-dense virtual machine featuring 2 vCPUs backed by a single physical Intel Xeon core operating at 2.8 GHz and 16.0 GB of RAM. With an elevated allocation of 8.0 GB of memory per vCPU, it is configured for applications requiring substantial memory without extensive parallel processing capabilities. The x86_64 CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AES, accompanied by a 33 MB L3 cache. The instance includes no integrated GPUs or local storage. In benchmark evaluations, it demonstrates moderate single-core capacity with a stress-ng score of 1827.69, while multi-core processing remains constrained by the single-core topology, scoring 1875.88. Large-block memory bandwidth reaches 13.86 GB/sec for uncached reads. This server is suited for lightweight in-memory databases, key-value stores, intermediate caching servers, and memory-sensitive background workloads.
